definitions.explanation: White, lightning-bolt-shaped paper strips attached to sacred ropes ({注連縄|しめなわ}), wands ({御幣|ごへい}), and other Shinto ritual objects to mark off purified or sacred space.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{紙垂|しで}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{下|さ}がっていた→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧。
examples.english: Paper streamers were hanging from the torii gate.

examples.japanese: ⟦{注連縄|しめなわ}→注連縄：06015_shimenawa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙垂|しで}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Paper streamers are attached to the sacred rope.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神主|かんぬし}→神主：16732_kannushi⟧さん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{紙垂|しで}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ついた{御幣|ごへい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}って→振る：01983_furu⟧{清|きよ}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{儀式|ぎしき}→儀式：00071_gishiki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}った→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The Shinto priest waved a wand with paper streamers attached to perform the purification ritual.

notes:
Pure Japanese reading despite the kanji compound. The zigzag shape is said to evoke lightning and to ward off evil.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙垂|しで}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}ける→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧: to attach paper streamers
- {紙垂|しで}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ついた⟦{注連縄|しめなわ}→注連縄：06015_shimenawa⟧: a sacred rope with paper streamers
- ⟦{白|しろ}い→白い：00587_shiroi⟧{紙垂|しで}: white paper streamers

CULTURAL NOTE:
Seen at shrines, on house entrances during New Year, around sumo rings, and on sacred trees. Together with ⟦{注連縄|しめなわ}→注連縄：06015_shimenawa⟧ they mark the boundary between everyday and sacred space. Several folding styles exist ({吉田流|よしだりゅう}, {白川流|しらかわりゅう}, {伊勢流|いせりゅう}) and the shape varies subtly by shrine tradition.
